The unqualified identification with that interface therefore omits a domain caveat. The new formula itself is well-defined even for an empty parameter set, where its universal requirements are vacuous, so this is nonfatal. The repair preserves that domain and identifies the nonempty case through D(y)={mu in M:tau(mu) in C(y)}: for every mu, its membership section is exactly the original section and hence has identical measurability and coverage.

The definition asserted a selected conditional-law conclusion without positive selection probability. With n=1, eta=1, A=(1,-1)^T and b=(0,0), S={0}, Z=0 and L=U=0; the nondegenerate normal density gives P_mu(S)=0 and Delta_vartheta(0)=0. Thus conditioning by P_mu(S) is undefined and the claimed selected probability is unavailable. The total zero-extended statistic is nevertheless well-defined. The repair qualifies only the conditional-law clause by P_mu(S)>0 and preserves every pivot formula and the null-event extension.
